$comment: Shared table for whitespace-keeping tag removal, read by go/strings_test.go (StripHTMLTags) and test/string.test.ts (stripHtmlTags) so neither language can drift. Each <...> span is removed and nothing is inserted in its place, which leaves an element's text content; every other character, whitespace included, passes through. This is the prose-carrying counterpart of StripHTML/stripHtml, which collapses whitespace runs and trims.

cases.input:
line vty 0 1
 access-class MANAGEMENT_NET in
 transport input ssh
cases.stripped:
line vty 0 1
 access-class MANAGEMENT_NET in
 transport input ssh
cases.why: line breaks and the indentation after them are data

cases.input:
ip access-list extended MANAGEMENT_NET 
permit ip x.x.x.0 0.0.0.255 any
deny   ip any any log-input
cases.stripped:
ip access-list extended MANAGEMENT_NET 
permit ip x.x.x.0 0.0.0.255 any
deny   ip any any log-input
cases.why: trailing spaces and interior runs of spaces are not collapsed
a blank line is a paragraph break
tab and NBSP pass through unchanged
an inline element leaves its text and the surrounding spaces
a tag span becomes nothing, not a space
a span runs from < to the first following >, as in StripHTML
a < with no closing > stays literal
